question: In March 2025, Prime Minister of India laid the foundation stone of National Referral Centre for Wildlife at ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Junagadh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **March 2025**, the **Prime Minister of India** laid the foundation stone of the **National Referral Centre for Wildlife** at **Junagadh**, Gujarat.
 
• The establishment of this centre aims to provide a **dedicated facility for wildlife conservation**, research, and management in India.
 
• **Junagadh** was chosen as the location due to its proximity to the **Gir National Park**, which is renowned for being the last natural habitat of the **Asiatic lions**.
 
• The **National Referral Centre for Wildlife** will play a critical role in addressing wildlife health issues, conducting research, and enhancing capacities for wildlife protection and care.
 
• It is part of the government’s broader agenda to strengthen **environmental conservation** and promote **sustainable development**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Junagadh:**

 
 
• **Junagadh** is a city in the state of **Gujarat, India**, located near the **Gir National Park**, the only habitat for the **Asiatic lions**.
 
• The city has a rich history, with several ancient monuments like the **Uparkot Fort** and **Junagadh Buddhist Caves**.
 
• Its proximity to the Gir forest makes it an important location for wildlife conservation and research activities.
 
 
 
• **Gir National Park:**
 
 
• The **Gir National Park** is a **wildlife sanctuary** located in Gujarat and is the **only remaining home of the Asiatic lions** in the world.
 
• The park spans an area of approximately **1,412 square kilometers** and is known for its diverse flora and fauna.
 
• It serves as a critical conservation area under the **Project Lion**, an initiative by the Indian government to protect the Asiatic lion population.
 
 
 
• **National Referral Centre for Wildlife:**
 
 
• The centre is envisioned to be a world-class facility for **wildlife disease diagnostics**, **veterinary care**, and **research on wildlife health**.
 
• It will focus on **preventive health measures**, treatment of injuries, and studying disease patterns in wildlife to ensure their safety and well-being.
 
• It will also serve as a training hub for **wildlife veterinarians** and researchers.
 
 
 
• **Other Locations:**
 
 
• **Kota**: Located in Rajasthan, it is famous for its coaching institutes and the **Kota Barrage**. It is not associated with wildlife conservation on a national scale.
 
• **Udaipur:** Known as the **City of Lakes**, it is a prominent tourist destination in Rajasthan but has no significant role in wildlife health research.
 
• **Bhopal:** The capital of Madhya Pradesh, it is known for its lakes and the **Van Vihar National Park**, but it is not the site for the proposed National Referral Centre for Wildlife.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wildlife Conservation in India:**

 
 
• India is home to a wide variety of **flora and fauna**, with over **7-8% of the world's biodiversity**.
 
• Several initiatives, such as **Project Tiger** and **Project Elephant**, have been launched to protect endangered species.
 
• The **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, provides the legal framework for wildlife conservation in India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Wildlife Health Centres:**
 
 
• Wildlife health centres are crucial for monitoring and controlling **zoonotic diseases** that can spread to humans.
 
• They also aid in maintaining the ecological balance by ensuring the survival of endangered species.
